newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke sticks by price target,would use rates.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke sticks by price target,would use rates.

text.p: Britain's finance minster Kenneth Clarke remains committed to the government's inflation target and is willing to change interest rates to hit targets.

"I stand ready to change interest rates. Up, down, whatever is necessary to hit the inflation target at what is the proper economic time," Clarke told the British Broadcasting Corporation's Money Programme on Sunday.
Figures released last week showed British underlying inflation remained above target, at 3.3 percent in the year to November, against the government target of 2.5 percent.

"It is important that Britain has good economic management that gives people confidence we are going to hit this low inflation target because that is the key part of keeping competitive," Clarke said in the BBC interview. He said that Britain's track record on inflation had improved immeasurably from the 1980s when inflation had been in double digits.
Clarke noted that from being one of the European laggards on inflation, Britain had improved.

"We (in Europe) are all very close together. I agree inflation is something you have to remain constantly vigilant about to have a permanent low inflation culture in the United Kingdom to keep up our present success," he said. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 7717
